rows.value_as_printed: down to 10 K (MAPEX instrument entry); testing at 20 K now possible at MPA Bremen (Leibniz-IWT)
rows.quote: By means of an integrated flow cryostat, specimens can be cooled to temperatures down to 10 K by means of liquid helium. | [IWT:] mechanical-technological materials testing at extremely low temperatures (20 K), which has recently become possible at the MPA Bremen.
rows.document_title: University of Bremen MAPEX instrument database: Cryo-static/dynamic testing HB100 (ZwickRoell, 2022); corroborated by Leibniz-IWT event page 'Leibniz-IWT Live: (Uncommon) Failure Analysis and (cryogenic) Material Testing at the MPA Bremen' (https://www.iwt-bremen.de/en/media/events/detail/nicht-alltaegliche-schadensansanalyse-und-kryogene-werkstoffpruefung-an-der-mpa-bremen)
rows.location: MAPEX page, 'Technical aspects' paragraph; IWT event page, paragraph on Dr.-Ing. Andree Irretier's 20 March 2025 talk
rows.reasoning: The facility entry documents a continuous-flow LHe cryostat cooling specimens 'down to 10 K' (lower bound 10 K = 10000 mK, vocabulary unit mK). The upper bound 20 K is the highest cryogenic operating point explicitly documented: Leibniz-IWT states 20 K mechanical testing became possible at MPA Bremen, the HB100's location (Building MPA, room 0190), presented by Irretier, the HB100's named application scientist. 20 K is a conservative documented point, not the cryostat's upper limit (ambient upper end is not stated for this unit, so it is not claimed). The interval covers the 20 K requirement.

rows.value_as_printed: cooled by means of liquid helium via integrated flow cryostat
rows.quote: The servo-hydraulic testing machine allows static/dynamic testing in tension/compression direction. By means of an integrated flow cryostat, specimens can be cooled to temperatures down to 10 K by means of liquid helium.
rows.document_title: University of Bremen MAPEX instrument database: Cryo-static/dynamic testing HB100
rows.reasoning: The facility's own technical description positively identifies the machine's cryogenic environment as a liquid-helium continuous-flow cryostat on a servo-hydraulic tester; the coolant/specimen medium is helium, not liquid hydrogen. ZwickRoell's own cryogenic page treats hydrogen-medium operation as a distinct configuration, and nothing for this instrument describes LH2 supply, LH2 immersion or hydrogen safety enclosure. Searched MAPEX entry, Leibniz-IWT hydrogen-technologies and event pages, Irretier's testXpo 2022 abstract and ZwickRoell cryogenic-testing page; none indicate LH2 handling on the HB100.

rows.value_as_printed: Measured quantity: stress-strain diagram, bending test, fracture mechanical properties
rows.quote: Measured quantity: Determination of stress-strain diagram, bending test, fracture mechanical properties (all up to 10K). Main application: Mechanical testing under cryogenic conditions up to 10K
rows.document_title: University of Bremen MAPEX instrument database: Cryo-static/dynamic testing HB100
rows.location: General information > Measured quantity / Main application; Techniques: tensile test
rows.reasoning: The facility entry enumerates the instrument's measured quantities and main application as mechanical (stress-strain, bending, fracture mechanics) testing; its technique is 'tensile test'. It is a servo-hydraulic mechanical tester, a different kind of instrument from a gas-permeation cell (no permeant gas supply, upstream/downstream pressure or leak/mass-spectrometric detection is part of its scope). Hence cryogenic gas permeation is not a function of this configuration.
